node.rich_text: In Python, a parameter is a variable name listed inside a function's definition parentheses, acting as a temporary placeholder for incoming data. While the terms are frequently used interchangeably in casual coding conversations, a parameter is the variable defined in the function signature, whereas an argument is the actual value or data object passed into that placeholder when the function is executed. This distinction is widely agreed upon by developers across coding communities like
